correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the two explicit factorial formulas in the archival Wronski-map source. After cancellation, the valuation difference is exactly F(ab)-F(ab/2)-sum(F(2t)-F(t)) over t from (a-b+1)/2 to (a+b-1)/2. Using F(2t)-F(t)=t, the sum is ab/2 because it is an arithmetic progression of b terms with endpoint sum a. Legendre's formula then yields the binary-digit expression. The bundled exact checker independently verifies both source formulas, the valuation equality, and the digit-sum formula over a broad finite range.

value.rationale: The complex Wronski degree is the total algebraic count of a central-projection fiber, while the real Wronski degree is a signed topological count that controls real solutions in real enumerative geometry and pole placement. Exact equality of their two-adic valuations says that passing from the complex count to the signed real count loses no additional power of two anywhere in the entire nonzero regime. This is a natural arithmetic comparison of two central enumerative invariants rather than a one-off congruence.
